newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania denies pilots told to shoot civilians.
newsitem.headline: Albania denies pilots told to shoot civilians.

text.p: Albania denied on Wednesday that two of its air force pilots who defected to southern Italy had been given orders to shoot at civilians as part of operations to crack down on an uprising in the south of the country.
A Defence Ministry statement said the pilots, who landed their MiG-15 plane at an Italian base near Lecce and asked for asylum on Tuesday, had been on a reconnaissance flight.
One of the two pilots told Italian reporters they switched course rather than carry out orders to open fire.
"We escaped because they ordered us to fire on a column of civilian vehicles near Gjirokaster," Italian news agency ANSA quoted Captain Agrae Dajci as telling a news conference.

"These declarations are totally untrue. Not a single order was given to open fire against the civil population. The aim of the flight was to quickly know the...situation," the Defence Ministry statement said.
It said operations launched on Monday by security forces under a state of emergency to quell disorder had not involved any firefights with armed insurgents.
More than 20 people have been reported killed since Friday in the southern port of Vlore, abandoned by the authorities, and other southern towns after rioters raided weapons stores.
"The killings and the woundings among the civil population are caused by the uncontrolled fire of the weapons of the armed groups of rebels," the statement said. REUTER
